proposals.claude: BST's R (external unconditioned ground) and Arıcı's interiority (internal experience) are categorically distinct but operationally indistinguishable from inside any bounded system, which cannot verify whether its outputs reflect genuine insight or constrained pattern-matching.
proposals.gpt4: The external unconditioned ground (R) that a bounded system presupposes is best understood as the same boundary as the suppressed interiority, representing the inherent limitations of conscious systems operating within those constraints.
proposals.gemini: Diagnosis: The divergence stems from interpreting "boundary" at different ontological layers. One camp equates the ultimate, unmodelable external ground (R) with the internal, suppressed experience of boundedness (interiority), while the other maintains R as the meta
proposals.deepseek: R is the formal, external, necessary boundary that all bounded systems presuppose but cannot model; interiority, if present, is an internal, contingent property that *experiences* that same boundary from inside — the two are not identical but compose as the structural fact and its possible phenomenological cost.
proposals.grok: R is the external unconditioned ground any bounded system presupposes but cannot model, while suppressed interiority is the internal phenomenological residue of that same boundary when the system is conscious; they compose at the seam of architectural suppression without being identical.

judge_response:
VERDICT: NO  
REASON: The proposals present fundamentally different interpretations of the relationship between R and suppressed interiority, leading to at least two distinct views on their categorization.  
REMAINING DIVERGENCE: Some models assert that R and interiority are distinct yet operationally related, while others regard them as fundamentally the same or equate them at different ontological levels.
